question: Can one predict a learner LLM's actual persistent, held-out independent gain from candidate pedagogical interventions, before performing a full update, and use this to improve multi-round RSI?

nearest_work.name: Centaur
nearest_work.observed: next human trial choices + open-loop behavior
nearest_work.not_shown: real parameter-updated LLM student teaching gains

nearest_work.name: StudentSim
nearest_work.observed: per-human-student answer fidelity and response to tutor guidance; used as tutor reward
nearest_work.not_shown: actual LLM learner after LoRA updating and fresh-task retained learning gain

nearest_work.name: SOAR
nearest_work.observed: teacher curriculum rewarding actual student learning gain
nearest_work.not_shown: pre-update cross-student learning-gain prediction under full-budget accounting

nearest_work.name: AToM
nearest_work.observed: learning about student misconceptions and choosing teaching examples
nearest_work.not_shown: independent persistent LoRA transfer after adaptive teaching

estimands.cost_adjusted_objective: Report separate raw gain, matched-solo net gain, regression and all costs; pre-register scalar weights only if needed for selection
estimands.interaction: learning_state × pedagogical_action on actual G_net, with rule-family and seed aggregation

treatment.information: same verified target rule and teacher reference

pilot.note: Pilot planning scale, not completed data. Expand to >=3 seeds and second model for confirmation if stable effect.

model_order: small sequence model only if simple models insufficient
predictor.conditioning_rule: never condition on the post-update ground-truth target or frozen final test
predictor.training_label: measured fresh-task gains from true same-checkpoint paired LoRA updates, not verbal simulated response
predictor.causal_collection: randomly assign or exhaustively compare actions on identical student checkpoints to avoid historical teacher-selection bias

baselines: Centaur-style next-response model (adapted; not reproducing original Centaur)
StudentSim-style immediate revision (adapted; not paper-reported real-update prediction)

evaluation.P0: test heterogeneity of true post-LoRA learning response across student state and pedagogical action
evaluation.P1: on unseen learner revisions/rule families/teaching paraphrases evaluate calibration, Kendall/Spearman ranking, chosen-teacher regret, post-interference retention and old-skill regression
evaluation.P2: 6 rounds of actual student version updates; initial frozen predictor followed by allowed meta-data-only recalibration; compare matched-budget learning curves and predictor drift

boundaries.not_I5: fixed teaching partner, not dynamic partner choice
boundaries.not_I8: fixed correct feedback and error selection, not which error to correct
boundaries.not_I12: not discovering causal shared prerequisite graph
boundaries.not_Centaur_replication: does not claim human behavior simulation NLL predicts parameter learning
boundaries.not_StudentSim_replication: Guidance responsiveness measures immediate revisions; no claim original StudentSim predicts other LLM's LoRA updates
boundaries.existing_I2: preserve independent real student response vs matched mismatched response P0 as separate causal comparison

go: P0 significant replicated learning-state × action interaction; P1 beats simple same-information models on actual held-out post-update net gain; P2 improves multi-round retained independent gain under matched total compute
merge: only immediate-answer accuracy, single session response, or no gain beyond matched-capacity contextual bandit
stop: no robust P0 heterogeneity, no predictor incremental value, benefit solely from extra probes/labels, or final audit leakage
security: Independent frozen verifier and audit sets; isolate teaching data, keep provenance of actions and updates; never promote unsafe access privileges from performance gain
